Muscular dystroglycanopathy from defective O-glycosylation; brain malformations or intellectual disability affect >30% across the spectrum; ocular damage is subtype-dependent.
Hereditary bradykinin-mediated angioedema affecting skin and subcutis; KNG1-associated disease is not an immune-mediated disorder.
Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy in 14/14 and skeletal deformities in about half; characteristic hypercholesterolemia in 9/12. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.
Defined by disease of the heart or pericardium; additional organs depend on the subtype.
Defining bilateral Duane anomaly, congenital myopathy and severe early scoliosis; motor delay does not establish additional neurologic disease.
Gonadal sex cord-stromal tumor with endocrine Leydig-cell differentiation, often producing androgens.
Palmoplantar keratoderma and esophageal neoplasia define this syndrome; oral leukoplakia also supports gastrointestinal involvement. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
GABRB3-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures and developmental impairment define the disease.
Defining cleft palate and absent dentition, stapes fixation with conductive deafness, and carpal/tarsal synostoses.
Acute leukemia of megakaryocytic lineage involving blood and bone marrow; no common additional organ damage established.
Neoplasm arising in salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
The syndrome combines renal tubular Fanconi dysfunction and neonatal hyperinsulinism; no evidence supplied for other commonly damaged organs.
Most angiomyolipomas arise in the kidney; hepatic and other extrarenal sites are minority locations. Tumor composition does not establish additional organ axes.
Defining camptodactyly, contractures and skeletal abnormalities with severe myopia and extraocular muscle fibrosis; facial and hairline features add no damaged organ.
Congenital neutrophil deficiency causes innate immunodeficiency; neutropenia and recurrent infections occurred in 4/4 patients.
Benign follicular epithelial neoplasm arising in the thyroid endocrine gland.
Defined by disease of the pharynx, included in the pulmonary axis; infectious or neoplastic mechanisms vary across subtypes.
Malignant embryonal tumor of the cerebellum; melanotic differentiation does not indicate a skin primary.
Congenital skin and hair depigmentation; white eyebrows and eyelashes are hair findings. Hearing, bowel and neurologic abnormalities each occur in <30%.
Malignant tumor involving kidneys or urinary tract; lymphoma and endocrine mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Microcephalic neurodevelopmental disorder with osteodysplasia and primordial dwarfism; both brain and skeletal abnormalities define the condition.
Neoplasm involving the conus medullaris of the spinal cord.
Disordered spinal autonomic control with defining episodes of severe hypertension; stroke is an uncommon complication. Bladder and rectal distention are triggers.
Skeletal dysplasia characterized by metaphyseal chondromatosis, including the humerus and femur.
